name: Diary studies and video missions (dscout)
summary: Join occasional paid research 'missions' where you record short videos and answer questions on your phone; this is not a job.
whatYouDo: You apply to missions in the dscout app by answering screener questions. If chosen, you complete mission parts, such as recording videos and answering questions about how you use products or go about daily life, and you're paid after the project closes.
appeal: Missions can pay tens to hundreds of dollars each (third-party reviews say about $20 to $200+)
You do it on your phone, on your own schedule within mission deadlines
dscout says it has scouts in the US, the UK and around the world, and the app is listed in the Canadian App Store
watchOuts: No official dscout page confirmed Canada eligibility in this check
Third-party reviews say mission availability depends on your location and demographics
Payment is PayPal only, about two weeks after the project's final mission closes, and you must claim the payment within 30 days
You record videos about your life and habits

compensation.notes: dscout says pay varies with each project's requirements and time. Third-party reviews give about $25–$150 per mission or $20–$200+ per study, without a stated currency basis for Canada.

reliability.notes: Missions depend on researcher demand and your demographics and location. No volume data was found.

fees: No dscout fee found; PayPal charges a small fee if you ask for a paper cheque instead.
applicationSteps: Download the dscout app and create a scout profile
Answer screeners for missions that interest you
If selected, complete each mission part by its deadline
Claim the PayPal payment (sent about 2 weeks after the project closes) within 30 days
fitsIf: You're comfortable recording short phone videos and want occasional, higher-value research missions.
notFitIf: You need confirmed Canadian access or regular income, or you don't want to film yourself.
